video_title: After the Ledger Hack and Quantum Warnings, Is Self-Custody ‘Slowly Dying’?
gist: Arc Invest's Lorenzo Valente argues crypto is moving from retail primitive-discovery to institutional, RWA-driven scaling, with self-custody losing to exchanges and ETFs amid the Ledger hack and quantum/AI cryptography fears. He also covers broken Ethereum L1 value accrual, skepticism of token buybacks, and bullishness on tokenized equities and Tether/Circle.

themes.theme: Crypto era shift to institutions and RWAs

insights.claim: The first era of crypto was about discovering primitives (AMMs, money markets, perps) with retail early believers as users; the next phase is one-to-100 scaling of proven protocols merging with TradFi, aimed at institutions and real-money use cases like payments, cross-border payments and trading.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Investable edge shifts from underwriting net-new protocols to picking incumbents that scale into institutional finance.

insights.claim: Arc considers its underwriting of Bitcoin, Ethereum and layer ones largely done, and sees the larger growth in applying crypto primitives to equities, fixed income, art, prediction markets and compute, asset classes orders of magnitude bigger than crypto.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Crypto-native companies that cannot extend onto off-chain asset classes risk being overrun.

insights.claim: AI is driving the cost of developing and integrating crypto toward zero, and large public companies with big balance sheets (Tether, Circle) are entering, so past crypto moats are far weaker and bootstrapping a competitor in six to twelve months is no longer easy.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Startups face tougher competition; scale incumbents compound advantages.

insights.claim: There is record consolidation, with a record number of crypto projects, protocols and applications closing and sunsetting; Abstract, a layer 2, is closing and giving users only a month to withdraw.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Expect more shutdowns and added abandonment risk for layer 2 and app holders.

insights.claim: Arc's barbell for crypto companies: winners either own the user relationship (exchanges, brokers) or are core infrastructure with huge TAM (Solana, Ethereum, Uniswap, Morpho); anything in the middle without user relationship or core infrastructure gets squeezed.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Use the barbell to screen crypto equities and tokens; avoid middleware squeezed in the middle.

themes.theme: Quantum and AI threat to cryptography

insights.claim: Roughly 70% of the questions Arc gets from RIAs and wealth-management platforms concern quantum, signature transition and which blockchain has the better roadmap, showing institutions treat it as a core allocation question.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Quantum readiness is becoming a diligence criterion for institutional crypto allocation.

insights.claim: Rapid AI progress, including a model solving the Navier-Stokes problem, has compressed Arc's planning timelines, making it hard to project beyond a few years and forcing thinking on 20 to 30 year horizons versus the usual 5 to 10 for venture.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Tail-risk of earlier-than-expected cryptographic breaks is being priced into institutional thinking.

insights.claim: Post-quantum signatures are not well tested and opinions diverge on them, and Bitcoin and Ethereum governance (miners, votes, community, stakers) may get lost in votes when the situation calls for founder-mode decisiveness, such as migrating before mid next year.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Governance speed, not just technology, is the main quantum risk for large L1s.

insights.claim: A quantum or AI-driven ECDSA break may go unnoticed because thefts could start slowly inside the existing noise of billions of dollars in yearly hacks, phishing and North Korean theft, unless a clear outlier spike appears.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Q-day may arrive without a clean signal, so waiting for proof before migrating is risky.

insights.claim: Open models that anyone can use make AI-driven attacks harder to control, and an attacker could secretly harvest data and attack later, so projects may become sitting ducks before crypto benefits from quantum.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Defensive benefits of quantum arrive after offensive risk.

insights.claim: Lorenzo is more positive on Bitcoin than a year ago: Arc is in a consortium with MicroStrategy and others talking to core devs, solutions are being drafted, and he expects a transition before Q-day, though what happens to Satoshi's coins is unresolved.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Reduces perceived Bitcoin quantum tail risk, with the Satoshi coin question as the residual.

themes.theme: Self-custody decline and exchange security as a moat

insights.claim: Arc's internal thesis is that self-custody is slowly dying: the marginal new crypto user will use Coinbase, Robinhood or ETFs rather than hardware or browser wallets, and the lack of self-custodying users is one reason DeFi is not growing.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Distribution and custody accrue to regulated intermediaries and ETFs rather than self-custody tooling.

insights.claim: Lorenzo would now recommend an ETF to a normie friend buying Bitcoin for the first time, and is himself consolidating custody he has self-held for years because keeping up with AI, quantum and protocol shutdowns is too hard.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Even sophisticated holders are shifting to institutional custody.

insights.claim: Security and regulation are becoming a moat for exchanges: a clean hack record, many licences, a public balance sheet and an emergency fund matter, and US exchanges look advantaged over European and Asian ones.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Favors regulated US-listed exchange equities; exchange custody diligence should include emergency fund size and incident history.

insights.claim: Most industry hacks have been at Asian exchanges, brokers and platforms, and large centralized exchanges are best positioned for quantum and AI because they can fund research and best-in-class security setups.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Supports preference for large, well-resourced custodians.

insights.claim: The hardware wallet market is structurally weak: Ledger, Trezor and Coldcard have all had several problems in two to three years, the market is niche with little revenue to attract big players, and the Ledger incident involved implanted custom hardware to steal seed phrases via an approved third-party vendor in Malaysia.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Supply-chain risk makes self-custody hardware a poor foundation for mass adoption.

themes.theme: Ethereum value accrual and L2 franchise model

insights.claim: Ethereum's value accrual is broken: about 99% of activity sits on five to seven layer twos (mainly Base and Robinhood), and Robinhood chain was making several million dollars a day while the Ethereum base layer accrued about $100 to $200.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: ETH cannot be valued on fee capture today; fundamentals lag the narrative.
insights.quote: Robin Hood was making several millions of dollars a day and basically Ethereum base layer was acrewing $100 like literally a hundred to $200

insights.claim: Ethereum functions like a franchise model (Base and Robinhood as McDonald's franchises) with growth no longer happening at the L1; the Foundation has not internalized this, and ETH has underperformed as the market prices it in.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Ethereum needs a strategic choice: scale L1 throughput or fully support L2s and capture their economics.

insights.claim: Tokenized equity trading volume is happening mostly on Solana, Base and Robinhood, so RWA growth may bypass the Ethereum L1, which could become a proof-posting/DA layer holding about 50 to 100 billion of stablecoins.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: RWA winners may not be ETH; watch where tokenized equity volume settles.

insights.claim: Lorenzo assigns a small but non-zero probability that Ethereum holds around $5 trillion of assets and is highly valuable without making money, like Bitcoin, but says he would not bet on it.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Store-of-value outcome for ETH is a tail scenario, not the base case.

insights.claim: Programmatic buyback-and-burn is overemphasized: early-stage startups using 100% of revenue for buybacks signal no growth path, and investors would rather see capital spent scaling the business, as AI startups get preempted rounds while crypto startups buy back tokens.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Treat 100%-revenue buybacks at young projects as a negative growth signal.
insights.quote: I think people have become crazy with this topic

insights.claim: Past buyback-heavy projects such as dYdX, OpenSea and Blur have faded, which suggests buybacks were a poor use of capital.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Historical precedent argues against buybacks as a durable support.

insights.claim: Lorenzo argues Hyperliquid should use its large market cap to acquire companies, including a joke-serious suggestion to buy Gemini in the US, as perps competition from Coinbase, Robinhood and Backpack intensifies and US-approved perps and stock perps arrive.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Hype's moat is tested by regulated US competitors; M&A could be a positive catalyst.

insights.claim: Making a buyback programmatic adds no credibility because the team can reverse it at any time; the real underwriting is team trust, and hard-coding such mechanisms early is a red flag.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Discount programmatic buyback claims when evaluating tokens.
insights.quote: Like if you have to encode some of this stuff like that early into the project, it's not good.

insights.claim: Lorenzo expects tokenized equities could surpass stablecoin on-chain supply within about three years; stablecoins are roughly 300 billion today and growing about 40%+ CAGR, but equities add a large new asset set and demand for US stocks offshore.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Tokenized equity infrastructure and distribution venues are the growth vector beyond stablecoins.

insights.claim: Stablecoins' real PMF today is exporting the dollar to emerging markets rather than payments or remittances, and tokenized stocks should follow a similar pattern of exporting US assets to other countries, with perps dominant before spot because spot requires custodians and clearing houses.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Expect perps on tokenized stocks to lead spot volume near-term.

insights.claim: Much crypto yield is circular, relying on leverage or looping ETH and Solana, so tokenized equities could add uncorrelated yield not tied to Bitcoin, ETH and Solana.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Diversifies DeFi yield sources.

insights.claim: Arc brought its venture fund on chain via Securitize with subscriptions and redemptions at the same public NAV on and off chain, but no secondary market yet; Arc frames crypto as a new distribution platform.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Early institutional template for tokenized funds; secondary liquidity is the next milestone.

insights.claim: Tether and Circle are protected by network effects and switching costs; Binance holds roughly 45 billion of USDT with no yield for over 10 years and has not switched even though rivals might pay 60 to 80% of net interest margin, so new stablecoins and consortiums are underestimated as hard to scale.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Incumbent stablecoin issuers keep their moat; Circle is evolving into a broader internet money company.

insights.claim: Neutrality matters: a Binance-issued stablecoin (Paxos partnership, shut down after regulator action) is unlikely to be adopted by others, and consortium stablecoins lack aligned incentives.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Supports Circle's independence as an advantage over exchange-owned or consortium coins.

insights.claim: Cloudflare reported that over 50% of internet traffic is now AI bots, and is exploring having agents pay nano-transactions for content access, which implies 10 to 100 million TPS, two to three orders of magnitude beyond current L1s such as Solana, Sui and Aptos.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Throughput is the key constraint and differentiator for L1s targeting agentic payments.

insights.claim: Current agentic commerce usage via MPP and the Coinbase and Circle x402 protocol is very nascent; layer zero is expected to launch an L1 in the next few months with impressive throughput.
insights.speaker: Lorenzo Valente (Arc Invest)
insights.so_what: Agent payments are a long-dated option rather than a near-term revenue driver.
